column3: doc
Media types the client can handle in the response, in order of preference.
Content encodings (compression such as gzip, br, zstd) the client understands.
Natural languages the client prefers for the response.
CORS: whether the browser may expose the response when the request was sent with credentials (cookies, HTTP auth).
CORS preflight answer: request headers the actual request may use.
CORS preflight answer: HTTP methods allowed for the actual request.
CORS: the origin allowed to read the response, or * for any origin (not allowed together with credentials).
CORS: response headers that scripts on other origins may read.
CORS: how many seconds the browser may cache a preflight answer.
Seconds the response has been in a proxy cache.
HTTP methods the resource supports; sent with 405 Method Not Allowed.
Advertises another way to reach the same service, e.g. HTTP/3 on a UDP port (h3=":443").
Credentials for authenticating the client to the server (Basic, Bearer token...).
Caching rules for browsers and proxies: max-age, no-cache, no-store, private, public, immutable...
Hop-by-hop options for this connection only, e.g. keep-alive, close, or upgrade for WebSockets; proxies do not forward it.
Whether content is shown inline or downloaded as an attachment, with an optional file name.
Compression applied to the body (gzip, br, zstd); the client must decode it.
Natural language of the intended audience of the body.
Size of the body in bytes.
Restricts which sources the page may load scripts, styles, images, frames and more from; the main defense against XSS.
Like Content-Security-Policy, but only reports violations instead of blocking them; useful to test a policy.
Media type of the body, e.g. text/html; charset=utf-8.
Cookies the browser sends back that were previously set with Set-Cookie.
Requires cross-origin resources to opt in (CORP or CORS) before the page may embed them; needed for cross-origin isolation.
Isolates the page's browsing context group from cross-origin windows that it opens or that open it.
Lets a resource refuse to be loaded by other sites or origins (same-site, same-origin, cross-origin).
Date and time at which the message was created.
Set to 1 when the request arrived in TLS 1.3 early data (0-RTT) and may be replayed.
Identifier of a specific version of the resource; used with If-None-Match for revalidation.
Expectations the server must meet, practically only 100-continue before the body is sent.
Date after which the response is stale; overridden by Cache-Control max-age.
Standard form of X-Forwarded-For/-Host/-Proto: client address, host and protocol as seen by proxies.
Host name and port the request is for; selects the virtual server. With proxy_pass, nginx sends the upstream's address unless you set it, e.g. proxy_set_header Host $host.
Makes the request conditional: only proceed if the resource's ETag matches.
Conditional request: send the body only if the resource changed after this date, otherwise 304.
Conditional request: send the body only if the ETag differs, otherwise 304 Not Modified.
Makes a Range request conditional on the resource being unchanged.
Hints for a persistent connection (timeout, max requests); hop-by-hop.
Date the resource was last changed; used with If-Modified-Since.
Links related to the resource, e.g. preload hints; also used by 103 Early Hints.
URL to redirect to (3xx) or of a newly created resource (201).
Scheme, host and port the request came from; the basis of CORS checks.
Enables or disables browser features (camera, geolocation, fullscreen...) for the page and its frames.
HTTP/1.0 caching hint; Pragma: no-cache. Superseded by Cache-Control.
Credentials for authenticating to a proxy server.
Requests only part of the resource, e.g. bytes=0-1023; answered with 206 Partial Content.
Address of the page that linked to the requested resource (the misspelling is standard).
How much referrer information the browser includes in the Referer header of later requests.
How long to wait before retrying, with 503 or 429 responses or redirects.
Software that produced the response; nginx's version can be hidden with server_tokens off.
Sends a cookie to the browser, with attributes such as Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite, Max-Age.
HSTS: tells browsers to use only HTTPS for this host for max-age seconds, optionally includeSubDomains and preload. Send it with always so error responses carry it too.
Transfer encodings the client accepts, e.g. trailers; required to be trailers for gRPC.
How the body is framed for transfer, e.g. chunked; hop-by-hop.
Asks to switch protocol on this connection, e.g. websocket. Hop-by-hop, so nginx must pass it explicitly: proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade.
Identifies the client software (browser, bot, library).
Request headers that change the response, so caches keep separate copies (e.g. Vary: Accept-Encoding).
Proxies the message passed through.
Authentication method the client must use; sent with 401 Unauthorized.
nginx-specific, set by the upstream: yes/no turns response buffering on or off for this response.
nginx-specific, set by the upstream: charset of the response.
nginx-specific, set by the upstream: seconds (or @unix-time) to cache the response in nginx; 0 disables caching.
nginx-specific, set by the upstream: limits the rate of sending this response to the client.
nginx-specific, set by the upstream: makes nginx serve an internal redirect to this URI instead, e.g. protected downloads.
nosniff stops browsers from guessing a different Content-Type than the one sent.
Client address followed by each proxy's address. Append the client with proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for.
Original Host requested by the client before a proxy changed it.
Protocol (http or https) the client used to reach the proxy; set it with $scheme.
Whether the page may be shown in a frame (DENY, SAMEORIGIN); superseded by CSP frame-ancestors.
Non-standard: the client's IP address as seen by the proxy, set with proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr; read back by the realip module.
Non-standard: unique ID for tracing a request through proxies and logs; nginx provides one as $request_id.
Obsolete browser XSS filter switch; modern browsers ignore it. Use Content-Security-Policy instead.
